He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest Demon Deacons]]. Born in [[Le Havre]], France, he began his career at [[INSEP]] in [[Paris]], competing with the amateur club [[Centre Fédéral de Basket-ball]] of the [[Nationale Masculine 1]] (NM1). He became among of the most sought-after prospects of the class of 2018, and a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], after moving to [[Wesleyan Christian Academy]] in [[High Point, North Carolina]]. ==Early life== Hoard was born in [[Le Havre]], France to an American father and French mother, both with [[basketball]] experience.{{cite web |title=France's Hoard has basketball family when he needs it |url=http://www.fiba.basketball/world/u17/2016/news/frances-hoard-has-basketball-family-when-he-needs-it |publisher=[[FIBA]] |accessdate=June 24, 2018 |date=June 23, 2016}} His father Antwon Hoard played for [[Murray State Racers men's basketball|Murray State]] in college and spent multiple seasons in France in the [[LNB Pro A]].{{cite web |last1=Jordan |first1=Jason |title=French import Jaylen Hoard acclimating himself to the U.S. style |url=http://usatodayhss.com/2016/elite-24-french-import-jaylen-hoard-is-acclimating-elite-24-under-armour-france-fibas-jaylen-hoard-wesleyan-christian-academy |publisher=USA Today High School Sports |accessdate=June 23, 2018 |date=August 19, 2016}} His mother Katia Foucade played for the [[Washington Huskies women's basketball|University of Washington]] and was a member of the [[France women's national basketball team|French national team]]. Hoard's younger sister Anaia, one of four siblings, has played with the [[France women's national under-17 basketball team|French national under-17 team]].{{cite web |title=Jaylen Hoard Bio |url=http://www.wakeforestsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/jaylen_hoard_1069364.html |publisher=Wake Forest Sports |accessdate=June 24, 2018 |archive-date=June 25, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180625185323/http://www.wakeforestsports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/jaylen_hoard_1069364.html |url-status=dead }} ==Youth career== In 2015, Hoard signed a two-year contract with the French athlete institute [[INSEP]] in [[Paris]], joining affiliated club [[Centre Fédéral de Basket-ball]] (CFBB).{{cite web |last1=Hein |first1=David |title=All in the family for INSEP's Hoard |url=http://www.adidasngt.com/u18/news/latest/i/6vn3ru86n4qfxrfw/all-in-the-family-for-insep-s-hoard |publisher=Adidas NGT |accessdate=June 24, 2018 |date=May 12, 2016}}{{cite web |last1=Halley |first1=Jim |title=France's Jaylen Hoard is a standout at Jordan Brand International Game |url=http://usatodayhss.com/2015/frances-hoard-is-a-standout-at-jordan-brand-international-game |publisher=USA Today High School Sports |accessdate=June 24, 2018 |date=April 17, 2015}}{{cite web |title=Quentin et Jaylen au Centre Fédéral à partir de septembre ! |url=http://www.bbc25.fr/2015/04/08/quentin-et-jaylen-au-centre-federal-a-partir-de-septembre/ |publisher=Besancon Basket Club |accessdate=June 24, 2018 |language=fr |date=April 8, 2015}} With CFBB, Hoard competed in the [[Nationale Masculine 1]], the [[French basketball league system|third-tier division]] in France, for the 2015–16 season.{{cite web |title=Jaylen Hoard Player Profile |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Jaylen-Hoard/Summary/89197 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |accessdate=June 24, 2018}} In April 2015, he was named [[most valuable player]] (MVP) of the [[Jordan Brand Classic]] International Game, recording 16 points, 7 rebounds, and 5 steals. On April 16, 2016, Hoard recorded a season-high 23 points, shooting 9-of-15 from the field, in a win over [[Caen Basket Calvados]].{{cite web |title=Apr 16, 2016 - Caen Basket Calvados vs. Centre Federal du Basket-Ball |url=https://basketball.realgm.com/international/boxscore/2016-04-16/Caen-Basket-Calvados-at-Centre-Federal-Du-Basket-Ball/216948 |publisher=[[RealGM]] |accessdate=June 24, 2018 |date=April 16, 2016}} He finished the NM1 season averaging 8.0 points, 3.5 rebounds, 1.6 assists, and 1.1 steals per game. ==High school career== In the summer of 2016, Hoard arrived in the United States to begin playing [[basketball]] for [[Wesleyan Christian Academy]] in [[High Point, North Carolina]].{{cite web |last1=Bossi |first1=Eric |title=North Carolina duo of Hoard and Wiggins turning heads |url=https://basketballrecruiting.rivals.com/news/north-carolina-duo-of-hoard-and-wiggins-turning-heads |publisher=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] |accessdate=June 24, 2018 |date=October 4, 2016}} He was encouraged to join the program because his father had become friends with its head coach [[Keith Gatlin]] during his playing career. After making the move, Hoard said, "I just felt like it was time to come over here and compete against the best. A lot of people know me for basketball in France, but I want to make it over here. This is where all the talent is so I want to prove myself." Entering the season, Wesleyan was ranked among the top-10 in the nation by [[MaxPreps]], and in the top-20 by ''[[USA Today]]'' High School Sports.{{cite web |title=High School Top 25 team preview: No. 10 Wesleyan Christian Academy |url=http://www.maxpreps.com/news/CnyT34WVPE-NezfZWCsHfw/high-school-top-25-team-preview--no-10-wesleyan-christian-academy.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |accessdate=June 24, 2018 |date=November 9, 2016}}{{cite web |last1=Halley |first1=Jim |title=Super 25 Preseason Boys Basketball: No. 20 Wesleyan Christian Academy (High Point, N.C.) |url=http://usatodayhss.com/2016/super-25-preseason-boys-basketball-no-20-wesleyan-christian-academy-high-point-n-c |publisher=USA Today High School Sports |accessdate=June 24, 2018 |date=November 2, 2016}} In the beginning of the season, he spent time adjusting to the American style of basketball.{{cite web |title=French import Jaylen Hoard not yet used to American basketball, still a top-30 recruit |url=http://usatodayhss.com/2017/french-import-jaylen-hoard-not-yet-used-to-american-basketball-still-a-top-30-recruit |publisher=USA Today High School Sports |accessdate=June 24, 2018 |date=January 9, 2017}} Hoard was rated as a five-star recruit and considered one of the best players of the 2018 class. at Wake Forest, Hoard averaged 13.1 points, 7.6 rebounds, and 1.5 assist per game. ==National team career== Hoard made his debut with the [[France national under-17 basketball team|French youth national team]] at the [[2015 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship]] in [[Kaunas]], Lithuania.{{cite web |title=Jaylen Hoard |url=https://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/123215/pid2//sid/11538/tid/282/tid2//_/2015_U16_European_Championship_Men_Division_A/index.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180625185601/https://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/123215/pid2//sid/11538/tid/282/tid2//_/2015_U16_European_Championship_Men_Division_A/index.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=June 25, 2018 |publisher=[[FIBA]] |accessdate=June 24, 2018}} In his first game at the event, he recorded 16 points and 6 rebounds to help defeat [[Croatia men's national basketball team|Croatia]].{{cite web |title=France vs. Croatia (Group D) |url=https://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/game/p/gid/1/grid/D/rid/11539/sid/11538/tid/282/_/2015_U16_European_Championship_Men/statistic.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151110210057/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/game/p/gid/1/grid/D/rid/11539/sid/11538/tid/282/_/2015_U16_European_Championship_Men/statistic.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=November 10, 2015 |publisher=[[FIBA]] |accessdate=June 24, 2018 |date=August 6, 2015}} At the tournament, he averaged 7.7 points, 4.0 rebounds, and 1.2 steals per game, leading France to a fifth-place finish. In April 2016, Hoard represented France at the [[Albert Schweitzer Tournament]], playing six games and averaging 7.0 points, 2.0 rebounds, and 1.3 steals per game, en route to fourth place. He was considered one of the top prospects from the event, although basketball website NBAdraft.net said that he "underachieved."{{cite web |last1=Bortoluzzi |first1=Davide |title=Albert Schweitzer Tournament: Top Prospects |url=http://www.nbadraft.net/albert-schweitzer-tournament-top-prospects |publisher=nbadraft.net |accessdate=June 24, 2018 |date=April 16, 2016}} However, Hoard drew attention later in the year, at the [[2016 FIBA Under-17 World Championship]], held in [[Zaragoza]], Spain. He averaged a team-high 22.4 points, 5.7 rebounds, 3.1 assists, and 1.7 steals per game, as France finished in sixth place. On June 23, 2016, in his opening game, Hoard erupted for 41 points against [[South Korea national basketball team|South Korea]], shooting 15-of-28 from the field. The performance tied the tournament's single-game scoring record set by [[Isaac Humphries]] in [[2014 FIBA Under-17 World Championship|2014]].{{cite web |last1=LeTourneau |first1=Nicholas |title=Top international prospects from the group stage of FIBA U17 |url=https://www.ridiculousupside.com/2016/6/27/12034096/top-international-prospects-from-the-group-stage-of-fiba-u17 |publisher=Ridiculous Upside |accessdate=June 24, 2018 |date=June 27, 2016}} ==Professional career== ===Portland Trail Blazers (2019–2020)=== Hoard went undrafted in the [[2019 NBA draft]]. On July 1, 2019, Hoard signed a two-way contract with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Sign Jaylen Hoard to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-sign-jaylen-hoard-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=July 1, 2019|access-date=July 2, 2019}} On October 27, 2019, Hoard was assigned to the [[Texas Legends]] of the [[NBA G League]] by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{cite web|title=TRAIL BLAZERS TRANSFER MOSES BROWN AND JAYLEN HOARD TO TEXAS LEGENDS|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/2019/10/27/blazers-transfer-moses-brown-jaylen-hoard-to-texas-legends|website=NBA.com|date=October 27, 2019|access-date=October 27, 2019}} Hoard participated in the [[2020 NBA Bubble]].{{cite web|title=Anthony Davis helps Lakers rout Trail Blazers to tie series|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=401236288|website=ESPN.com|date=August 20, 2020|access-date=August 20, 2020}} ===Oklahoma City Thunder / Blue (2021–2022)=== On December 4, 2020, Hoard signed with the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], but was waived three days later.{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Thunder Sign, Waive Jaylen Hoard|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2020/12/thunder-sign-waive-jaylen-hoard.html/|date=December 9, 2020|website=HoopsRumors.com|accessdate=December 9, 2020}} On January 28, 2021, he was included in the roster of the [[Oklahoma City Blue]].{{cite web|title=Oklahoma City Blue Announces 2020-21 Roster|url=https://oklahomacity.gleague.nba.com/news/oklahoma-city-blue-announces-2020-21-roster|website=NBA.com|date=January 28, 2021|access-date=January 28, 2021}} In 15 games, he averaged 9.7 points, 4.9 rebounds and 2.0 assists in 22.0 minutes per contest while shooting 49.1 percent from the field.{{cite web|title=Thunder Signs Jaylen Hoard to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/hoard-210405|website=NBA.com|date=April 5, 2021|access-date=April 5, 2021}} On April 5, 2021, the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] signed Hoard to a [[two-way contract]]. Hoard rejoined the Oklahoma City Blue for the 2021–22 season.{{cite web|title=Back in Blue: Oklahoma City Blue composite guide|url=https://bricktownbeat.com/2021/11/04/back-in-blue-oklahoma-city-blue-composite-guide/|website=BricktownBeat.com|date=November 4, 2021|access-date=January 8, 2022}} On December 29, 2021, Hoard signed a 10-day contract with the Thunder{{cite web|title=Ready for the Call|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/ready-for-the-call-211230|website=NBA.com|date=December 30, 2021|access-date=December 30, 2021}} and returned to the Blue after it expired.{{cite web|title=2021-2022 Oklahoma City Blue Transactions History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/dleague/teams/Oklahoma-City-Blue/38/Transaction_History/2022|website=RealGM.com|access-date=April 1, 2022}} On April 1, he signed a second 10-day contract with the Thunder.{{cite web|title=Thunder Signs Jaylen Hoard to 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release-hoard-220401|website=NBA.com|date=April 1, 2022|access-date=April 1, 2022}} On April 6, 2022, he recorded career highs of 24 points and 21 rebounds against his former team, [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{cite web|title=Top Performers: Jaylen Hoard Impresses as Trio of OKC Blue Members Star Versus Trail Blazers |url=https://www.si.com/nba/thunder/news/top-performers-jaylen-hoard-impresses-as-trio-of-okc-blue-members-star-versus-trail-blazers|website=si.com|date=April 6, 2022|access-date=April 6, 2022}} ===Hapoel Tel Aviv (2022–2024)=== On August 14, 2022, Hoard signed with [[Hapoel Tel Aviv B.C.|Hapoel Tel Aviv]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]].{{Cite web |date=2022-08-14 |title=Jaylen Hoard joins Hapoel Tel Aviv |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/eurocup/1377663/hapoel-tel-aviv-adds-jaylen-hoard-eurocup/ |access-date=2022-08-15 |website=Eurohoops |language=en}} On July 31, 2023, he signed two-year extension with the club. '''Maccabi Tel Aviv (2024–present)''' In July 2024, Hoard signed with [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]] of the [[EuroLeague]] and the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]]. == National team career == Hoard was on the [[France men's national basketball team|France national team]]'s preliminary roster for the 2024 Olympics.{{Cite web |title=France announce 14-man list for Paris Olympics, cut two players |url=https://basketnews.com/news-208835-france-announce-14-man-list-for-paris-olympics-cut-two-players.html |access-date=2025-09-08 |website=basketnews.com |language=en}} He played at [[EuroBasket 2025]] and averaged 8.4 points and 3.8 rebounds per game.{{Cite web |date=2025-09-07 |title=Jaylen Hoard (France) - Basketball Stats, Height, Age {{!}} FIBA Basketball |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/players/218682-jaylen-hoard |access-date=2025-09-08 |website=www.fiba.basketball |language=en}} == Personal == Hoard's mother, Katia Foucade Hoard, played [[point guard]] at [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington]] and was on the [[France women's national basketball team|French women's national team]] at the [[1994 FIBA World Championship for Women]]. She returned home to France and played professionally as well.{{Cite news |last=Brown |first=C.
